## ROOT repair directive — angle 0 v2

**Decision: REVISE, not terminal.** The product-scale lower-bound kernel remains viable, but the flagship experiment must be replaced with Gu–Yin–Cai–Fan’s exact fixed-class experiment. Do not try to rescue the present “observed-code minimax frontier” comparison through prose. A bridge would be a separate, substantial theorem and is unavailable in the current proposal.

### 1. Replace the risk and its quantifiers

Delete `Γ_n(b_n)`, `R_n(b_n)`, the code spaces, code variables, jointly measurable decoding machinery, `def:observed-code-minimax-risk`, and every “observed-code” or “common-code” headline.

Reproduce Gu et al.’s objects faithfully:

\[
\mathcal T_3=\{f\in L^2(\nu_d):\|f\|_\infty\le3\},
\]

\[
\mathcal H_n(\bar\delta)=
\left\{
F\subseteq\mathcal T_3:
\exists G\subseteq\mathcal T_3,\
\sup_{f\in F}\inf_{g\in G}\|f-g\|_{L^2(\nu_d)}
\le\delta^{\rm appr},\
\sup_{\delta\ge\delta^{\rm stoc}}
\frac{\mathcal R_{n,\nu_d}(\delta;\partial G)}{3\delta}
\le\delta^{\rm stoc}
\right\}.
\]

Distinguish the **truth class** \(F\) from its **learner-class witness** \(G\); the current artifact incorrectly replaces Gu’s uniform truth-class condition by an instancewise condition on \(P\).

Define the exact Appendix A.1 family

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal P_{\rm Gu}(F_\mu,F_\pi)=\{P_{\beta,v,\mu,\pi}:&
\ X\sim\nu_d,\quad \mu\in F_\mu,\quad \pi\in F_\pi,\\
&T=\pi(X)+u,\quad E[u\mid X]=0,\quad
E[u^2\mid X]\equiv v\ge1/3,\\
&Y=\beta T+\mu(X)+\varepsilon,\quad
E[\varepsilon\mid X,T]=0,\\
&|\beta|\vee|v|\le3,\quad |T|\vee|Y|\le3\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Then use Gu’s quantifier order exactly:

\[
m_{\rm Gu}(n,\bar\delta_\mu,\bar\delta_\pi)
=
\sup_{F_\mu\in\mathcal H_n(\bar\delta_\mu)}
\sup_{F_\pi\in\mathcal H_n(\bar\delta_\pi)}
\inf_{\widehat\beta}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\rm Gu}(F_\mu,F_\pi)}
E_{P^{\otimes 2n}}|\widehat\beta-\beta(P)|.
\]

The infimum occurs **after** the fixed class pair is selected. Thus \(\widehat\beta\) may be tailored to and know \(F_\mu,F_\pi\), their learner witnesses, and the budgets. Gu’s outer supremum is not a random or hidden class choice.

Gu Appendix A.1 explicitly uses this fixed-class order and a \(2n\)-sample risk; its upper bound therefore applies to this \(m_{\rm Gu}\), not to the current jointly measurable observed-code risk. [Gu et al., Appendix A.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.06368v1)

### 3. Do not pursue the observed-code bridge in this revision

The generic minimax inequality goes in the unhelpful direction:

\[
\inf_{\delta(\text{class},D)}\sup_{\text{class}}\sup_P R
\ \ge\
\sup_{\text{class}}\inf_{\delta_{\text{class}}}\sup_P R.
\]

Consequently, Gu’s upper bound for the right-hand fixed-class risk does not upper-bound the broader observed-code risk. A valid bridge would need, at minimum, a uniform jointly measurable selection theorem producing class-tailored estimators with Gu’s rate over the entire coded class universe, plus an exact identification of the coded families with \(\mathcal H_n\). That is new mathematics, may fail for arbitrary standard-Borel codings, and distracts from the product-converse kernel. Replace the broader risk rather than asserting this bridge.

The causal potential-outcome layer may be retained only as an optional lemma showing that the constructed hard subclass admits a constant-effect causal extension. It must not redefine or narrow the headline comparator silently.

## Root repair directive

**REVISE by separating the literal Appendix A.1 display from the paper’s apparently intended mean-zero PLM. Do not call the proposal’s mean-zero family or risk “Gu’s exact Appendix A.1 family/risk.”**

The literal equation (A.1) really displays
\[
E[\varepsilon Y\mid X,T]=0,
\]
with \(Y\) multiplying \(\varepsilon\). It is not typeset as a subscript, the error is introduced as \(\varepsilon\), and no \(\varepsilon_Y\) notation is defined. The paper’s main model (1.1) and its earlier minimax family (3.2), however, both impose \(E[\varepsilon\mid X,T]=0\). Thus the extra \(Y\) is very likely a typographical error—not an \(\varepsilon_Y\) convention—but this cannot be silently corrected or quoted as the literal content of (A.1) without an author correction or erratum. [Gu–Yin–Cai–Fan, equations (1.1), (3.2), and (A.1)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.06368).

The literal condition is mathematically different. If
\[
a(X,T)=\beta T+\mu(X),\qquad Y=a+\varepsilon,
\]
then it says
\[
aE[\varepsilon\mid X,T]+E[\varepsilon^2\mid X,T]=0.
\]
Consequently, combining it with mean-zero error would force \(\varepsilon=0\) almost surely.

More decisively, the literal model destroys identification even in the proposed non-atomic subclass. Take
\[
F_\mu=F_\pi=G_\mu=G_\pi=\{0\},\quad
T=u\sim {\rm Unif}[-1,1],\quad v=1/3,\quad
Y=0,\quad \varepsilon=-\beta T .
\]
These singleton classes are admissible at every stated budget, \(T\) is bounded and non-atomic, and \(E[\varepsilon Y\mid X,T]=0\). Yet every \(\beta\in[-3,3]\) induces the same observed law. Hence either \(\beta(P)\) is not a well-defined functional of the law, or, treating the parameterizations as labeled experiments, every estimator satisfies
\[
\max_{\beta\in\{-3,3\}}E|\widehat\beta-\beta|\ge3.
\]
This contradicts Theorem A.1’s vanishing upper bound at zero budgets. Therefore the literal equation cannot consistently support the claimed fixed-class rate frontier. Under a literal reading, the product-converse question is terminal: it is either ill-posed or trivially implied by constant nonidentification, not a sharp product-rate tightening.
